back: Semantic: class per pixel. Instance: separate mask per object. Panoptic: class per pixel plus instance id for countable things.
Encoder halves resolution and doubles channels; bottleneck; decoder upsamples and concatenates same-resolution encoder maps (skips); final 1x1 conv to classes.
H and W divisible by $2^D$ for $D$ downsampling stages.
They restore localisation detail lost when the encoder shrinks the feature maps.

front: Transposed conv vs bilinear upsample + conv
back: Transposed conv is learnable but can give checkerboard artefacts; bilinear + 3x3 conv has fewer artefacts and parameters.
Logits $(N,C,H,W)$, target $(N,H,W)$ of class ids; per-pixel cross-entropy averaged over $N,H,W$.
$2|P\cap Y|/(|P|+|Y|)$; soft version $2\sum p y/(\sum p+\sum y+\varepsilon)$; loss $=1-$Dice.
Cross-entropy gives stable gradients early; Dice optimises overlap and ignores background size. $L=L_{CE}+\lambda L_{Dice}$.

front: Mean IoU from a confusion matrix
back: $\mathrm{IoU}_c=M_{cc}/(\text{row}_c+\text{col}_c-M_{cc})$, then average over classes; also report per-class values.
Backbone + FPN, RPN proposals, RoIAlign, box head (class + refinement) and mask head (per-class low-resolution binary mask).
RoIPool rounds coordinates (misalignment up to a feature cell); RoIAlign keeps real coordinates and samples bilinearly.
Blend four neighbours: $(1-w_y)(1-w_x)f_{00}+(1-w_y)w_xf_{01}+w_y(1-w_x)f_{10}+w_yw_xf_{11}$; exact for linear $f$.
RPN objectness + RPN box + box classification + box regression + per-pixel binary cross-entropy of the mask.
